tagline: Trat's island arc — car-ferry dependency and an emerging island-hopping network.
summary: Koh Chang is Thailand's second-largest island, in Trat province near the Cambodian border. Access today is via car ferries from Laem Ngop; onward island-hopping to Koh Mak, Koh Kood and Koh Wai runs from Bang Bao. It is a frontier/roadmap market — strong scenic and resort demand, but longer mainland crossings that range-gate to Pioneer II hops or LR for the Bangkok link.

demand_signals.detail: Mu Ko Chang marine national park draws steady resort and eco-tourism flow.
Bang Bao is the hub for the Koh Mak / Koh Kood / Koh Wai archipelago.

navier_fit: Medium. Intra-archipelago hops fit Pioneer II well; the mainland car-ferry role is harder to displace. Frontier market — sequence after Samui/Pattaya prove out.
competitive_landscape: Car ferries (Centrepoint, Ferry Koh Chang) from Laem Ngop; wooden island-hopping boats from Bang Bao — no premium electric option.
seasonality: Peak: Nov-Apr. Strong SW monsoon May-Oct closes many island-hopping routes; tight seasonal gating.
regulatory_note: Thai cabotage + Marine Department licensing; proximity to Cambodia border adds maritime-zone caution for routing.

grab.super_app_fit: Grab island-hopping bundles from Bang Bao; resort transfer booking with GrabCar mainland handoff at Laem Ngop.
grab.wedge: Premium, quiet island-hopping in a marine national park — eco-positioning that diesel boats can't match.

transit_planning.note: Frontier/roadmap market; longer mainland link needs LR or stays ferry-served.

_enrichment.note: Connected city brief hung off the Koh Samui / Gulf flagship. Geometry sealed via Grok from Bucket-C BP files.
